requested.title: errorRate counts only transport failures, so the verdict's error gate cannot fire on any HTTP error status
Latency-creep gate silently cannot fire for runs shorter than 120s
CLI numeric arguments are unvalidated, so a typo yields a bogus verdict instead of an error
All five page fixtures use slashless paths, so the harness only exercises the trailing-slash redirect and never renders a page
Server-island fixture targets a development-only route while the harness runs the server in production mode, so the island endpoint is never exercised
Form fixture sends no Origin header, so it would be rejected by production CSRF even after the trailing slash is fixed
api:cookie fixture body does not match the route's expected JSON shape
Synchronous spawnSync('ps') every 2s blocks the same event loop that generates load and measures latency
kill() resolves as soon as SIGKILL is dispatched rather than after the child exits, and fires a stray SIGKILL after a clean shutdown
Shared cursor plus contiguous ring layout makes all concurrent workers hit the same route at once instead of a mixed workload

parsedVerdicts.reasoning: Verified line by line. In `loadGen.ts`, `stats.totalErrors` is incremented at exactly one site — L128, inside the `catch` around `fetch` — and that catch is only reachable for transport/abort failures. Any response that arrives takes the success path: L113-121 bucket it into `status2xx/3xx/4xx/5xx`, L122 increments `totalRequests`, and `totalErrors` is never touched. `runLeakTest.ts:167` then computes `errorRate = totalErrors / (totalRequests + totalErrors)`, so the ratio is structurally 0 for a server answering 500 on every request. I grepped for every consumer of `status5xx`: only `report.ts` (`summarizeWorkload` L63-65, `printReport` L107) reads it, purely for display. `VerdictInput` in `analyze.ts:74-80` has no status fields at all, so `judge`'s `if (input.errorRate > 0.005)` gate (analyze.ts:134) can only ever fire on transport failures. The README (L77) explicitly promises 'Also fails on: error rate > 0.5%', which the code does not deliver for HTTP errors. This is not merely theoretical: because of F4 and F5, roughly 68% of the default workload is 301/308 redirects and another ~4% is 404s, all of which land in `status3xx`/`status4xx` and count as successes, so `errorRate` is 0 and the run exits 0. HIGH_BUG is the right severity for a CI regression gate that cannot distinguish a wholly broken server from a healthy one. The recommendation (surface 5xx separately, carry an `expectStatus` per `RouteHit` since `page:error-404` and `unmatched:404` legitimately expect 4xx) is sound.

Confirmed exactly. `runLeakTest.ts:163` takes `latenciesBetween(stats, workloadStart, workloadStart + 60_000)` and L164 takes `latenciesBetween(stats, workloadEnd - 60_000, workloadEnd)`. `latenciesBetween` (loadGen.ts:49) filters `s.t >= fromMs && s.t < toMs`. For `--duration` under 60, `workloadEnd - 60_000 < workloadStart` and `workloadStart + 60_000 > workloadEnd`, so BOTH windows contain the complete sample set — they are literally identical, `lastWindow.p95 / firstWindow.p95` is exactly 1, `latencyCreepPct` is exactly 0, and the `latencyCreepPct > 50` gate at analyze.ts:139 provably cannot fire. For 60 < duration < 120 the windows overlap partially, so the signal is attenuated rather than fully suppressed — a small overstatement in the finding's framing of 'shorter than 120s', but the ≤60s case is an exact, provable dead gate. At exactly 120 (the value in the README's own flags example, L20) the windows are precisely disjoint and adjacent, so the harness sits on the boundary. The finding's observation that the code warns about short-run unreliability only for RSS sample count is also correct: L156-160 warns on `workloadSamples.length < 3` and nothing warns that a fail gate has been disabled. The default `--duration=600` is unaffected, which correctly keeps this at BUG rather than HIGH_BUG.

Verified. `parseArgs` is called with `strict: true` but every numeric option is declared `type: 'string'`, so strictness validates flag names and shapes only, never numeric content. L37-41 then coerce with bare `Number()` and nothing checks the result. I traced `--duration=abc` all the way through: `duration: NaN` → `durationMs: NaN` at L130 → `endAt = Date.now() + NaN = NaN` at loadGen.ts:82 → `Date.now() < NaN` is false, so every one of the 13 workers exits on its first loop test with zero requests. L146 `trimMs = Math.min(30_000, Math.floor(NaN/4))` = NaN (Math.min propagates NaN), so `trimStart` is NaN and the L148 filter `s.t >= NaN` matches nothing — `workloadSamples` is empty. Crucially the run does NOT bail: `rssSamples` is non-empty because the 60s default warmup already ran the poller, so the L150 throw is skipped; baseline and final probes both succeed so L153 is skipped; L156 only warns. `judge` then gets an empty sample array — `leastSquares` returns all zeros, `workloadSamples.length >= 5` is false so the monotonic-growth gate is skipped, `errorRate` is 0 (both totals are 0), and `latencyCreepPct` is 0 (firstWindow.p95 === 0). Verdict: PASS, exit 0. One correction: `--port=abc` is less silent than implied — `PORT="NaN"` reaches the site, where `Number(process.env.PORT) || 3333` falls back to 3333, so the readiness fetch to `http://127.0.0.1:NaN` fails until the 30s `bootTimeoutMs` and `startServer` throws. The finding only claims the NaN fetch URL, which is literally accurate. BUG is the right severity for operator-error robustness in a dev script.

Confirmed end-to-end against current HEAD (1cb3f3ce). `packages/site/src/index.ts:172` sets `trailingSlash: 'always'`; `KIND_POLICY.page.trailingSlash` is true (requestSetup.ts:63); `mirrorsSlashForm` causes Mochi.ts:1546-1553 to register the alt-slash variant so Bun matches the slashless form; and the page handler's `wrapRequest` (Mochi.ts:961-971) calls `buildRequestContext` as its very first statement, where the trailing-slash check at requestSetup.ts:107-117 is the first early exit — before CSRF, the cookie jar, protection, middleware, or any render. `isSlashExempt` (trailingSlash.ts:5-7) exempts only `/` and paths matching `/\.[^./]+$/`; none of `/demos/hello-world`, `/demos/data-loading/pikachu`, `/demos/server-island`, `/demos/error/404` contain a dot, so all five page fixtures get a 301 (GET) or 308 (POST) from trailingSlash.ts:53. `loadGen.ts:105` sets `redirect: 'manual'`, so the harness never follows them, and L116-118 bucket them as `status3xx` while L122 still counts them as successful requests — which is exactly why F1 keeps the verdict green. I verified the site registers no `trailingSlash:redirect` filter (its only filter is `consoleLogger:line`, index.ts:245-247) and no middleware rewrites the URL, so nothing mitigates this. Ring math: 7 routes at weight 1 (10 slots) plus `unmatched:404` at 0.3 (3 slots) = 73 slots, so ~68.5% of the default workload is pure redirect responses. Two supporting details in the finding are inaccurate and I note them for the record: (a) `warmup: { enabledInProd: true }` (index.ts:196) plus Mochi.ts:2127-2135 renders every static page pattern once at boot using the canonical slashed path, and a production run loads the registry from the manifest, so `compiledComponents`/`clientFiles`/`cssFileUrls` are NOT empty; (b) `unmatched:404` falls through to `composedFetch`, which renders the configured error page via `renderErrorResponse` (Mochi.ts:1911-1918), so that ~4% of traffic does SSR a Svelte component. Neither touches the core defect: the five page fixtures never re-render their pages under load, the form action never executes, and island props are never re-sealed. The repo's own CLAUDE.md warns about precisely this trap. HIGH_BUG stands.

Confirmed. `captureServerIslandHit` (routes.ts:41) fetches `/__leak/server-island`. That pattern is registered only via `...(DEVELOPMENT ? leakTestRoutes : {})` at `packages/site/src/routes.ts:385`, with `DEVELOPMENT = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'` (routes.ts:89). `runLeakTest.ts:83` passes `env: { MOCHI_MEMORY_PROBE: '1', NODE_ENV: 'production', PORT: … }`, and `serverProcess.ts:37` spreads it as `{ ...process.env, ...opts.env }` so the override wins. So the route is absent, the fetch 404s, `!res.ok` returns null (routes.ts:42-44), and L97 drops `island:server` from the mix entirely. The failure is non-fatal: L98-100 only `console.warn` and the run continues to an authoritative verdict. I confirmed the warning is genuinely invisible in practice — the server is spawned with `stdout: 'inherit'` and the site runs `logger: { level: 'log' }` with consoleLogger active, so a default 660s run at 50 rps buries that single line under tens of thousands of request lines, and because the route is never added to the ring it does not even appear with a zero count in `printReport`'s per-route table. The readiness check is unaffected because `/__mochi/health/memory` is gated on `MOCHI_MEMORY_PROBE === '1'` alone (Mochi.ts:1816), not on `development`, so the harness boots cleanly and gives no other hint. The impact assessment is right: `/_mochi/island/:componentName` (Mochi.ts:1559+) runs `decryptProps`, compiles islands on demand to `<outDir>/svelte-compile/<Name>-<hash>.server.js`, and dynamically imports them into a never-evicted module cache — the single most leak-prone path, and the one this harness exists to cover. I also verified the finding's side-note: `svelteAstPreprocess.ts:300` and :318 both emit `component-name="…" signed-props={…}` in that order, so `SERVER_ISLAND_RE` matches today but is order-fragile. Note the inline-budget path (:306-323) only triggers inside a nested island-endpoint render, so a top-level page render still emits the matchable placeholder. Gitignored reports in `scripts/leak/reports/` dated 2026-05-02 show `island:server` at 3447 2xx, but those predate this repo's initial commit (2026-05-18) and reflect a harness/site state not in git — they are not evidence about current code. HIGH_BUG stands.

Verified as a latent defect, correctly scoped by the finding itself to 'even after the trailing slash is fixed'. Today the 308 from F4 fires first, so CSRF is never reached; once the fixture path gains its slash, the trace is: `KIND_POLICY.page.csrf` true (requestSetup.ts:63) → `csrfCheck` at requestSetup.ts:120 → `DEFAULT_PROTECTED_METHODS` contains POST (csrf.ts:26) → `isFormContentType('application/x-www-form-urlencoded')` true (csrf.ts:60-68) → `expectedOriginConfigured` true because index.ts:201 sets `proxy: { origin, … }` → L149-155: `request.headers.get('origin')` is null (routes.ts:19 sets only Content-Type), so `originNormalized` is null and both pass-branches at L153 and L156 are skipped → `development` is false because the harness forces `NODE_ENV=production` → `csrfForbidden` returns 403 at L171. I also confirmed the compounding mismatch: index.ts:115-118 computes `origin` from `MOCHI_PORT`/`MOCHI_DOMAIN`, which the harness never sets, so `resolveExpectedOrigin` (proxy.ts:58-60) returns the literal `http://localhost:3333` while the harness listens on 13333 via `PORT` — so even a self-origin header would mismatch. And the resulting 403 lands in `status4xx` and is counted as a success (loadGen.ts:117-122), so F1 keeps the verdict PASS. The page does declare a `default` action returning `redirect(303, …)` (`packages/site/src/demos/data-loading/routes.ts:7-17`), so there is a real code path being skipped. This is a distinct defect at a distinct location from F4 (missing header on lines 13/16/19 vs slashless path), so it is not a duplicate. BUG is right — it is currently masked and only bites after F4 is fixed.

The core claim is definitively true. The fixture posts `JSON.stringify({ name: 'leak-test', value: 'x' })` (routes.ts:27) while `/api/cookie` destructures `const { username, theme } = (await request.json()) as { username: string; theme: string }` and calls `cookies.set('mochi_username', username, …)` / `cookies.set('mochi_theme', theme, …)` (`packages/site/src/demos/cookies/routes.ts`). Both values are `undefined` at runtime; the `as` cast is why typecheck stays green. CSRF does not block it — `isFormContentType('application/json')` is false (csrf.ts:60-67), so the handler runs. I resolved the ambiguity the finding left open, without executing anything: `MochiCookieJar.set` performs no validation (cookies.ts:96-100) and `serializeCookie` takes the options branch, building a `CookieInit` with `value: undefined` and passing it to `new Bun.Cookie(init)` (cookies.ts:37-56). `bun-types/bun.d.ts:10745-10758` declares `CookieInit.value?: string` as optional, so a missing/undefined value is a supported input rather than a constructor error — the route will not throw and will not 500. The gitignored 2026-05-02 report corroborates this: `api:cookie` shows 3566/0/0/0 (all 2xx). So the finding's second branch ('throws and yields a 500', 'the harness could be 500-ing on an eighth of its traffic') is unsupported and I am explicitly rejecting it; the real outcome is two meaningless `Set-Cookie` headers per request. The defect that remains is real and worth the stated fix: the fixture does not exercise what the README claims ('JSON API + MochiCookieJar' with real values), and the cookie-serialization path it does exercise is the degenerate empty-value one. Confidence 'medium' in the original was appropriate for the consequence; the mismatch itself is high-confidence. BUG — arguably a nit, but the fix is a one-line fixture change.

The code facts are fully confirmed: `sampler.ts:1` imports `spawnSync` from `node:child_process`, `sampleRss` (L15) calls it synchronously, and `startRssPoller` (L33-34) drives it from a `setInterval` at the 2000ms cadence passed by `runLeakTest.ts:88`. That interval runs on the same single event loop as `startLoad`'s 13 workers (loadGen.ts:138) and the `performance.now()` latency measurements at loadGen.ts:93/109. So the instrument does block the thing it measures — that part is not disputable, and for a harness whose only output is a latency-and-memory verdict the fix (`Bun.spawn` with awaited output, `/proc/<pid>/statm`, or a separate Worker) is clearly correct. I do want to correct the magnitude, because the finding overstates it twice. First, in-flight concurrency is `rps × latency`, i.e. roughly 0.25-2.5 requests at 50 rps with single-digit-to-tens-of-ms latencies — not 13 — so each ~5-20ms block inflates on the order of 300 samples out of ~30,000 in a default run (~1%), which moves p99 far more than the p95 the gate reads. Second, the claim that the contamination 'is not even uniform across the first-window and last-window comparison' does not hold: the sampler cadence is a fixed 2s and the request rate is fixed, so both 60s windows absorb the same ~30 blocking events and the perturbation largely cancels in the `lastWindow.p95 / firstWindow.p95` ratio at analyze.ts:139. The secondary note is accurate and correctly labelled cosmetic: `out.status !== 0` (L16) returns null for a missing `ps` too (status is `null`, not 0), so the operator sees `runLeakTest.ts:151`'s 'ps did not return any output' rather than 'ps not found' — on Windows that is the path taken. Keeping BUG, which is already the lowest severity available.

The described semantics are exactly right. `serverProcess.ts:65-68` does `proc.kill('SIGTERM')` then `await Promise.race([proc.exited, Bun.sleep(3000).then(() => proc.kill('SIGKILL'))])`. `Subprocess.kill()` returns synchronously once the signal is dispatched, so the sleep branch's `.then` callback resolves the moment SIGKILL is sent — the race settles there without ever awaiting `proc.exited`. `runLeakTest.ts:208` awaits this inside `finally` and L215 then calls `process.exit(code)`, so the harness can and does terminate while the child is mid-teardown. I verified the 3s branch is the COMMONLY taken one, not an edge case: `Mochi.serve()` installs a SIGTERM handler (Mochi.ts:2216) whose shutdown path waits `options.shutdownTimeout ?? (development ? 0 : 5_000)` — 5000ms here, since the harness forces `NODE_ENV=production` and the site sets no `shutdownTimeout` — and a non-forced `server.stop()` will not drain while the harness's own `keepalive: true` sockets (loadGen.ts:104) are still open, so `proc.exited` reliably resolves later than 3s. Practical harm is modest, which is why BUG is the right severity: SIGKILL is uncatchable and the kernel releases the port within milliseconds, and an orphan is reaped by launchd/init, so the 'next run fails its isPortInUse precheck' scenario needs a child wedged in uninterruptible I/O. The 'stray SIGKILL after a clean shutdown' sub-claim is weaker still — in the SIGTERM-succeeds path `process.exit()` at L215 fires before the pending 3s timer, so the stray signal is effectively unreachable dead code. The real defect is that a `finally`-block cleanup advertises confirmed teardown and does not provide it; the proposed `setTimeout` + `await proc.exited` + `clearTimeout` fix is correct.

The two code observations are accurate — `buildWeightedRing` (routes.ts:62-65) does push a route's slots contiguously with no interleave or shuffle, and `worker` (loadGen.ts:87-88) does read `opts.routes[(cursor + workerId) % len]` off a single shared `cursor` — but the failure mode they are claimed to produce does not occur, so the finding's headline is wrong. I worked the arithmetic out exactly. All 13 workers are started by one `Array.from(…, i => worker(i))` and each runs synchronously up to its first `await fetch`, so the first burst is: worker 0 reads cursor 0 and takes index 0 (cursor→1), worker 1 reads 1 and takes index 2 (cursor→2), worker k takes index 2k, worker 12 takes index 24. The shared increment plus the `+ workerId` offset yields an effective stride of 2, not 0 — so a burst of 13 requests spans 25 ring slots, i.e. about 2.5 of the 10-slot route blocks, hitting three distinct routes (5/5/3) rather than one. Each subsequent burst advances by `concurrency` (13), so with a 73-slot ring (7 routes x 10 slots + `unmatched:404` at `Math.round(0.3*10)` = 3) the harness sweeps every route in ~6 bursts. At the default `perWorkerIntervalMs = 1000*13/50 = 260ms` that is a full sweep roughly every 1.5s — shorter than the sampler's own 2s RSS interval (runLeakTest.ts:88) and ~40x shorter than the 60s latency windows at runLeakTest.ts:163-164. So neither the regression that `judge` gates on nor the p50/p95 windows can see a per-route sawtooth, and the finding itself concedes long-run proportions are correct (I confirmed: gcd(13,73)=1, so the window start walks every offset and coverage is uniform). Separately, actual in-flight concurrency is `rps x latency` — under ~2.5 requests at 50 rps — so there is no fleet of 13 simultaneous same-route requests to change which allocations are concurrently live. A shuffle or per-worker stride would still be a tidier design, and the degenerate low-rps case (`concurrency` floor of 4 at loadGen.ts:68 gives 4 adjacent slots per burst and a ~4.5s sweep) is worth keeping in mind, but neither supports the stated defect or its stated impact on the verdict.
